title: Bounds, Benefits, and Bad Air: Net Benefits of Pollution Alerts
abstract: Though air-quality alert systems (AQAS) cover more than 1.7 billion people worldwide, there has been little analysis of the net benefits of these systems. This paper presents a theoretical framework for deriving lower bounds on the net benefits of an AQAS and applies it to a South Korean system currently covering over 51 million people. Estimating a regression discontinuity design, we find that an alert issuance reduced youth respiratory expenditures by 30% and adult cardiovascular expenditures by 23%. The overall system reduced externalised health expenditures by 28.6 million dollars during 2016−2017, with a minimum benefit-cost ratio of 7.1:1. Including dynamic impacts of alerts increases the minimum benefits (benefit-cost ratio) to 36.7 million dollars (9.2:1). Our findings imply that the AQAS generates significant net benefits and suggests that manipulation of air quality data, which has been observed in other contexts, may negatively impact social net benefits.
abstract_zh: 尽管空气质量预警系统（AQAS）覆盖了全球超过17亿人口，但对这些系统的净收益分析却很少。本文提出了一个理论框架，用于推导AQAS净收益的下界，并将其应用于一个目前覆盖逾5100万人口的韩国系统。采用断点回归设计，我们发现预警的发布使青少年的呼吸系统支出减少了30%，成年人的心血管支出减少了23%。在2016至2017年间，整个系统使外部化的健康支出减少了2860万美元，最低收益成本比为7.1:1。若纳入预警的动态影响，最低收益（收益成本比）将提高至3670万美元（9.2:1）。我们的研究结果表明，AQAS产生了显著的净收益，并表明在其他情境中已被观察到的空气质量数据造假行为，可能会对社会净收益产生负面影响。

title: Do Environmental Markets Improve Allocative Efficiency? Evidence from U.S. Air Pollution
Fossil Fuels and Fiscal Federalism: How Intergovernmental Transfers Respond to Local Coal Industry Declines
Industrial Decline Raises Juvenile Antisocial Behavior: Evidence from US Coal Communities
abstract: This paper studies how coal production declines affect youth antisocial behavior in coal-dependent U.S. counties. Using county-level arrest and school-finance data, I find that coal busts are followed by higher arrest rates across age groups, with larger proportional increases among juveniles, especially for status offenses such as truancy. The busts coincide with school revenue shortfalls and cuts to operational spending, notably reductions in instructional aides and non-classroom support staff. I find little evidence that policing resources or family/child-abuse measures move in tandem with the bust. Overall, coal declines appear to raise crime generally while plausibly amplifying juvenile-specific impacts through school-finance pressures.
abstract_zh: 本文研究了煤炭产量下降如何影响依赖煤炭的美国县的青少年反社会行为。利用县级逮捕和学校财政数据，我发现煤炭行业萧条之后，各年龄段的逮捕率都有所上升，其中青少年的比例增幅更大，尤其是逃学等身份犯罪。这些萧条恰好与学校收入短缺以及运营支出削减同时发生，特别是助教和非课堂支持人员的减少。我发现，警务资源或家庭/虐待儿童措施的变化与萧条并没有同步发生的明显证据。总体而言，煤炭行业衰退似乎普遍推高了犯罪率，同时可能通过学校财政压力放大了针对青少年的影响。
